citations.description: Evidence report: 'The evidence is incomplete. Both deletions are confirmed present in the working tree, but whether they were landed as two separate, independently-revertible commits cannot be determined from the repository file contents alone — that information lives exclusively in git history, which is inaccessible to these tools.'

findings.criterion: Each deletion is a separate commit so either can be reverted independently
findings.detail: The evidence explicitly states that git history is inaccessible (`.git` directory not accessible to review tools) and no proxy artifact (CHANGELOG entries, commit message files, trailer-annotated files) was found to confirm the two deletions were landed as separate, independently-revertible commits. The working-tree state confirms both deletions exist, but the commit structure cannot be verified.
findings.remediation: Provide git log output (e.g., `git log --oneline -10`) or a CHANGELOG/commit-message artifact that records the two separate commits for the `bug_close_reason_ok` deletion and the `_attestation.py` deletion respectively.
findings.title: Commit separation not verifiable from repository file contents

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[operator-attested]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify.
